summary: Tested the inventory 'Compté par' traceability feature in the backend and the UI. Backend: 4 of 4 pytest tests pass. They cover how count_log is appended and deduplicated, a joint count by admin, a TEST_ stock_keeper and the manager, the submit/reject/close flow, and the 403 returned to non-owners on create and surprise. UI (admin and manager) works end to end: the inv-counters banner, the inv-counted-by-i column (name and date/time), the 'non enregistré' label while dirty, the column updating right after Enregistrer, the expandable 'N saisies' history, and owner-only buttons. One real issue: concurrent /count calls lose updates (1 lost write in 50 parallel requests).

minor.issue: Race condition. The endpoint reads the whole lines array, changes it in memory and writes it back with $set. When two counters save at the same moment, even on different lines, one save overwrites the other. Reproduced with tests/race_iter103_counts.py: 9/10 lines kept in 1 of 5 trials, all requests returned 200. This hits exactly the joint-count scenario the feature is for. Fix: per-line atomic update ($set lines.{i}.qty_counted/counted_by/counted_at + $push lines.{i}.count_log), or a version check with retry.

issues: An inventory created with product_ids (no scope) shows 'Tout le stock' in the subtitle. Misleading, cosmetic only.

action_items: Make inventory_count atomic per line (positional $set/$push, or optimistic concurrency) so simultaneous saves by the owner and the manager are not lost
critical_code_review_comments: inventory_count: the read-modify-write of the whole lines array causes lost updates when saves are concurrent (see above).
A count cannot be cleared back to null: the qty_counted null/'' value is silently ignored, so an accidental count can only be changed, not removed. Acceptable, but worth knowing.
Counters banner groups by display name (e.by), not by_id. Two staff members with the same name would be merged.

success_rate.backend: 100% (4/4 functional tests); concurrency probe failed (1 lost update in 50 writes)

seed_data_creation: Only TEST_ product, inventories and a stock_keeper user, all deleted afterwards. The manager and the TEST_ user were punched in through /attendance/check-in.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Staff login is at /console/connexion (not /console/login), using page.locator('input:visible').nth(0/1). Run pytest with -n 0. ui_seed_iter103.py creates the TEST_ inventory (line 0 counted by admin then manager); pass the argument 'cleanup' to remove it. Check-in pin must be digits only, so omit it.
